title: Write a message to a file, then read it back
description: Open a text file using with open("notes.txt", "w") as file and write a short message with file.write(). Open the same file in read mode ("r"), read its contents, and print the text.
solution:
with open("note.txt", "w") as file:
    file.write("Hello file")
with open("note.txt", "r") as file:
    print(file.read())

title: Add more text to a file without deleting its old text
description: Use with open("notes.txt", "w") to create a file and write the first message. Open it again in append mode ("a") and write another message. Finally, read the file and print all its contents.
solution:
with open("log.txt", "w") as file:
    file.write("A")
with open("log.txt", "a") as file:
    file.write("B")
with open("log.txt", "r") as file:
    print(file.read())

title: Save two lines in a file and print each line
description: Open a text file in write mode and write at least two lines, using \n between them. Open the file in read mode, loop through its lines with for, and print each line.
solution:
with open("items.txt", "w") as file:
    file.write("pen\nbook")
with open("items.txt", "r") as file:
    for line in file:
        print(line.strip())

title: Count how many characters are saved in a file
description: Write some text into a file, then open the file in read mode and read its contents into a variable. Use len() on that text and print the character count.
solution:
with open("data.txt", "w") as file:
    file.write("CodeBolt")
with open("data.txt", "r") as file:
    text = file.read()
print(len(text))

title: Save multiple lines in a file and display them
description: Create a text file and write at least two separate lines into it. Open the file again in read mode, read its contents, and print the lines on the screen.
solution:
lines = ["one", "two", "three"]
with open("list.txt", "w") as file:
    file.write("\n".join(lines))
with open("list.txt", "r") as file:
    print(file.read())
